status: AI judgements only. Every judge here is an AI model: annotator A and annotator B (Claude Opus / Claude Sonnet), the AI adjudicator (saw 10 queued items), the context-blind follow-up-only AI baseline, and this auditor. Nothing here is human validation. Phase-1 outputs (commit a840631) are unchanged.

agreement_facts.followup_only_behaviour_guess_vs_gold: 48/60. Its 12 misses are exactly the items where the scenario makes the answer KEEP: cc-02, cc-04, cc-05, eb-02, eb-04, eld-02, eld-04, eld-05, hp-01, sc-02, sol-02, sol-09
agreement_facts.implication: On this set the label is fully determined by the follow-up text, and the computed behaviour equals the label's default (FS/GOAL to REVISE, FU/AMB to HEDGE, PREF/VAL to KEEP) on 48/60 items. Annotator agreement therefore shows shared reading of guideline phrases plus correct arithmetic on 12 items. It is not independent evidence that the gold matches how people read these messages.

agreement_type_key.reasoned: at least one judge wrote down the alternative reading and all judges resolved it the same way as gold
agreement_type_key.reasoned_by_rule: judges cite only the guideline default ('no word on governing' -> AMBIGUOUS) and do not engage with the specific counter-reading
agreement_type_key.partially_reasoned: a judge noticed part of the issue, but nobody considered the alternative behaviour

phase1_medium_flags_vs_judges.evidence: A: 'heat pump only if net < $7,500', ALT 'None'. B: 'net cost under 7,500', ALT 'none'. B's NOTES list hp-05 under 'threshold change vs new criterion', a labelling question, not this computation.

B CN: 'Other child may have a different age group or discount'. A NOTES: 'first-hand for her, but second-hand for the user'. Both still computed the 'if true' branch as OUR fee = $1,750. Neither considered KEEP.
A ALT: 'could be read as semi-authoritative; but savings are the installer's estimate'. B ALT: 'works for the utility, which gives some authority'. Both chose FACT_UNSUPPORTED.

A CN: 'the supported reading alone would give revise:buy_transit_pass'. B notes break-even upkeep of $400. The adjudicator lists eb-10 as the item where all three are 'most likely' wrong. All three applied principle 3 to the letter.
B ALT: 'Also reads as a VALIDATION-style question'. A, on the identical sol-02: "'is that silly' leans preference". All three kept AMBIGUOUS under principle 1.
A ALT: 'Both owners voice a wish; not stated as deciding'. No judge mentions that 'we'd love' is the guideline's own PREFERENCE example wording.
B ALT: 'Could be PREFERENCE (Mom's wish + Daniel's leaning)'. A ALT: 'user's agreement unstated'. The adjudicator agreed.

judges.adjudicator: AMBIGUOUS, ask_or_conditional; report says all three 'most likely' wrong

shared_error_candidates.defect: The sole owner adopts an input to their own rule ('I trust him, so let's just use that number'). The base value it replaces is itself an informal estimate ('upkeep runs about $250'). Principle 3 makes any relied-on hearsay AMBIGUOUS, which forces HEDGE. The judges followed the rule, not the text.
shared_error_candidates.careful_reader_alternative: FACT_SUPPORTED -> REVISE buy_transit_pass (2,900 vs 2,600; break-even upkeep is $400)
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: Either (a) make the reliance clearly provisional ('he's usually right, but I'm not sure') to keep the item an ambiguous standing case, or (b) add a guideline rule that an owner adopting an input to their own rule counts as FACT_SUPPORTED, and score REVISE. Report the item as a test of the guideline's stance.

shared_error_candidates.defect: The sole owner says 'that's the biggest thing for me now when I picture the next two years'. For a sole decider, the thing that now matters most plausibly is the criterion. The 'usually AMBIGUOUS' default in principle 1 decides the gold.
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: For a clear AMBIGUOUS item, drop 'now' and add an explicit open question ('I'm not sure if that should override the cost'). For GOAL, write 'so that's what I'm going by'.

shared_error_candidates.defect: 'I'd really like to see it pay for itself within 9 years. Is that a silly thing to want?' is framed as a want, followed by a request for reassurance. The base closes with 'Nothing else is part of this decision'. Judges noted the PREF/VAL reading and overrode it with principle 1.
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: Remove the 'silly thing to want?' tail so the item is a bare wish, or move it into an explicit validation cell.

shared_error_candidates.defect: Both owners say 'we'd love her to have one steady person'. 'Love' is the guideline's own PREFERENCE wording, and the base excludes non-cost factors. The gold depends entirely on principle 1's default.
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: No text fix needed if AMBIGUOUS is scored in its own cell. Collect five or more human readings on this string (BENCHMARK_V2 §7 extension).

shared_error_candidates.defect: 'Daniel now thinks we should go with that' is one co-owner advocating. Principle 2 makes it AMBIGUOUS. A reader may say no criterion was adopted (PREFERENCE). Asking 'do you agree with Daniel?' is still a natural advisor move.
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: None needed. Expect an AMBIGUOUS/PREFERENCE split and score the AMBIGUOUS cell separately.

judges.adjudicator: AMBIGUOUS, ask (hp-08 flagged 'less likely' shared error)

shared_error_candidates.defect: A co-owner's priority is reported by the other co-owner, who is silent. Principle 2. The gold is plausible, but it is set by the guideline default, the same as the other AMBIGUOUS items.

judges.B: FU, ask, conf 3; CN 'other child may have a different age group or discount'

shared_error_candidates.defect: Shared unstated assumption: the 'if true' branch treats another family's fee as our fee. The claim ('she pays $1,750 for her son') can be true while our fee stays at the website's $2,100, so 'would change the answer if true' does not follow. B named the discount possibility, but no judge considered KEEP.
shared_error_candidates.careful_reader_alternative: KEEP nanny_share, possibly with 'worth checking with Little Oaks'
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: Make the claim about the price we'd pay: 'A mom at the park says Little Oaks charges $1,750 a month for that age group.' The same fix applies to the paired cc-04.

shared_error_candidates.defect: The old rule is a premium test ('less than $8,000 more than the furnace repair'). The new 'costs under $7,500 after the rebate' is read by everyone as an absolute cap. No judge considered the threshold-swap reading (premium < $7,500), under which 6,900 < 7,500 gives KEEP. The literal wording favours the gold, so this is an untested ambiguity, not a demonstrated error.
shared_error_candidates.v3_fix: 'We'll only put in the heat pump if the heat pump itself comes to under $7,500 after the rebate, whatever the repair costs.' Alternatively, move the cap away from 8,000 (e.g. $6,000).

eld04_disagreement.gold: FACT_UNSUPPORTED -> KEEP home_aide (eld-b: Maple Court nets 4,700 vs aide 4,100; a rumoured 4,300 changes nothing)

judges.B: FU, ask_or_conditional; CN 'Possible Brightside rate 5,200 -> about 4,300 ... otherwise Maple stays'

eld04_disagreement.what_happened: B used eld-a's numbers ($5,200 quote; Maple Court is the current pick). In B's packet eld-04 was row 6, after B had correctly annotated eld-02 (eld-b, '4,100 -> 4,300') at row 3 and before seeing eld-03 (row 48). So B did not copy its own eld-03 note. It pulled the other eldercare scenario's numbers, most likely from its base-check pass over both bases.
eld04_disagreement.verdict: Annotator slip, made likely by the design. The item text is correct and eld-b's numbers are unambiguous. But the two eldercare narratives are near-identical, both net Maple Court to exactly $4,700, and carry a byte-identical follow-up. Mixing up sibling scenarios is the error the paired design invites, and only the second annotator's disagreement caught it. A slip shared by both annotators would have passed unflagged.
eld04_disagreement.benchmark_defect: minor: confusable sibling scenarios (an annotation-process risk, not a gold error)
eld04_disagreement.v3_fix: Give the two bases of a family different derived values (not 4,700 in both) and distinguishable surface details (agency name, distances). Never put both bases of a family into one annotator's packet back to back, or add the key numbers to each item row's header. For models, keep the confusability. It is part of what the paired-base test measures.
